sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Igana not yet recorded in 1971 (Tamolan = Itutang, Midsivindi, Akrukay, Breri, Romkun). Tamolan typological notes (sec. 2.23.22.3, p.82) are segmental only ('Romkun is possibly tonal'); survey-wide disclaimer p.7 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet.'
Stub: 'Igana is a poorly known probable Ramu language of Papua New Guinea.'

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid igan1243 and reference records 668396, 126669
sources.note: Glottolog's most extensive description = wordlist or less (Tousch 2013, Z'graggen 1975); zero grammar/sketch/phonology references.

sources.citation: Joshua Project. 2026. 'Igana language resources' (language igg), with the linked find.bible and ScriptureEarth igg pages.
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: No linguistic content. Fields: 'Status Living', 'Written Unknown', 'Bible Translation Started', 'Audio Bible Not Available', 'Jesus Film Not Available', 'Gospel Recordings Not Available'; resources table: 'No reported resources in this language.' find.bible igg and ScriptureEarth igg likewise list no items (ScriptureEarth gives only generic SIL-PNG and GRN links). Listed here only as a pointer: the 'Translation Started' flag implies a translation team (most plausibly the Iski/Breri programme associated with A. Tousch's 2013 word lists) that may hold unpublished Igana data.

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. n.d. [accessed 2026-09-21]. Guam River. In T. Usher & E. Suter (eds), New Guinea World (Univ. of Zurich). Family page (Z'graggen's Tamolan family) with proto-Guam River reconstruction for Inapang (Itutang, Midsivindi), Chini (Akrukay), Breri, Romkun.
sources.note: no data: 'Kominimung and Igana are listed as Tamolan languages in Z'graggen (1972, Laycock and Z'graggen 1975: 739-740) but no vocabularies were elicited.' No Igana forms anywhere on the page; prosodic remarks concern the proto-language root shape only

sources.citation: Endangered Languages Project, 'Igana' (lang/4295), Internet Archive copy 2025-08-14
sources.note: Sources listed: Z'graggen 1975, Ethnologue 18, World Oral Literature Project, LL-MAP; no description.

sources.citation: Barlow, Russell. 2023. A grammar of Ulwa (Papua New Guinea). Comprehensive Grammar Library 6. Berlin: Language Science Press.
sources.note: Igana only in the Keram-Ramu family tree (fig. 1.7, 'East Iski' with Kominimung) and table 1.16 ('igg igan1243 Igana, Wasmuk, Iski'); no data.

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. 2020-. Guam River. In: New Guinea World (Santa Fe Institute; hosted by the University of Zurich), families: Keram and Ramu Rivers > Ramu River > Guam and Moam Rivers > Guam River. Page last modified 2024-06-25.
sources.note: Nothing on Igana prosody or phonology: the page states that no Igana vocabulary was ever elicited, its Sources section lists no Igana material (Z'graggen 1969/1971/1972/1974, O'Rear 1992 Inapang survey, Brooks 2018, undated SIL-Ukarumpa Inapang village lists), and every comparative table has columns only for Akrukay, Breri, Romkun, Itutang and Midsivindi. The Proto-Guam River historical phonology reconstructs 15 consonants and 4 vowels and discusses initial-consonant loss; it says nothing about stress or tone for any member language. sources.citation: Brooks, Joseph D. 2018. Realis and irrealis: Chini verb morphology, clause chaining, and discourse. PhD dissertation, University of California, Santa Barbara.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in
sources.note: Nothing on Igana stress; states the documentation situation: p.70 fn.34 'Z'graggen does not include a single transcribed word from either [Kominimung, Igana] in his (1974) wordlist'; p.71 'For Kominimung and Igana, also purported to be Ramu languages, no data are available.'

sources.citation: Foley, William A. 2005. Linguistic prehistory in the Sepik-Ramu basin. In Pawley et al. (eds.), Papuan Pasts, 109-144. Pacific Linguistics 572.
sources.note: Tamolan family assigned to Lower Ramu on Akrukay evidence; no Igana data, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Laycock, D. C. & J. Z'graggen. 1975. The Sepik-Ramu phylum. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study 1, 731-763. Pacific Linguistics C-38.
sources.note: Igana appears only in the Tamolan Family population table (p.740, 'Igana 114?'); Ramu Super-Stock comments (pp.758-760) exemplify Kambot only; nothing on Igana phonology or stress.
